answer: Think of the agent economy as a garden: a sybil attacker plants a vine of fake identities overnight, hoping sheer numbers crowd out real work. Bind each epoch answer to a sequential time-lock — a verifiable delay function over the epoch seed that takes minutes of real wall-clock time per identity and cannot be parallelized. One gardener can tend one meadow plot at a time; a thousand fake vines still need a thousand sequential waits, so mass identity creation buys no speed and the attack withers on its own cost.
